packs.title: Landmarks and City Life
packs.promise: Explore New York’s harbor, skyline, parks and cultural landmarks.

q.s: Make space for a quiet, respectful reflection.
st: Check current memorial access and choose a comfortable position clear of other visitors.
Pause quietly for a minute without seeking a photograph or particular emotional response.
After leaving the immediate memorial area, write one sentence about what you chose to pay attention to.

q.s: Make a small composition from cables and stone.
st: Use the signed pedestrian approach and move only as far as comfortable.
Choose a safe stopping position where a cable line and a tower edge share your view.
Draw their relationship in a small frame, keeping the walking route clear.

q.s: Notice how a short elevated path changes the city view.
st: Check the official map and current elevator information before choosing an entrance.
Walk a comfortable short out-and-back segment on the open path.
Compare one planted detail and one building edge from two stopping positions without blocking others.

packs.title: A Day Inside Central Park
packs.promise: Follow bridges, gardens and small stories through the park’s southern half.

q.s: Draw it with only five lines; decide which single line makes it recognizable.
st: Choose an open path view of the bridge without standing in its busiest crossing.
Frame a tiny scene using the bridge, water and one distant building.
Draw it with only five lines; decide which single line makes it recognizable.

q.s: Add one similarity and one difference between how the figures are presented.
st: Follow an open section of the promenade and choose two named monuments.
Record each name and one visible gesture or object, without guessing a biography.
Add one similarity and one difference between how the figures are presented.

q.s: Record the landmark that helped you keep the correct shore on your return.
st: Use the official park map to identify Bow Bridge and a return path toward Strawberry Fields.
Cross on foot or wheels if the bridge route suits you, or take an open lakeside route around it.
Record the landmark that helped you keep the correct shore on your return.

packs.title: Hidden in Plain Sight
packs.promise: Seventeen tiny missions. Two wild days. Seven citywide rituals.

q.s: Turn the classic DUMBO skyline into a four-layer composition puzzle.
st: Go to Pebble Beach at Main Street in Brooklyn Bridge Park.
Without moving anything, frame pebbles or granite, river, bridge, and skyline as four stacked bands.
Take one photo with all four layers visible.

q.s: Find the woman whose work helped carry an impossible bridge across the finish line.
st: Walk the Brooklyn Bridge pedestrian promenade and find the plaque naming John, Washington, and Emily Roebling.
Frame the plaque so Emily's name is the largest readable name and a bridge cable crosses the composition.
Save one fact about Emily that you want to remember.

q.s: Find the Chinatown block where Manhattan's geometry appears to glitch.
st: Find the Doyers Street sign at either end of the block.
Move only along legal pedestrian space until the street's hard bend makes the far end disappear.
Capture the readable DOYERS sign and the vanishing curve in one frame.
